newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet picks up on regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet picks up on regional demand.

text.p: Jet fuel firmed on Tuesday amid strong regional buying while gas oil edged down as the market came under renewed selling pressure in the face of prompt oversupply, traders said.

A major sold on Monday a 25,000-tonne jet fuel cargo to China at $2.05 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes for late February arrival on a cost-and-freight basis, up about 20 cents from the last traded level.
Jet fuel supplies are expected to remain tight and are not expected to get much boost from additional supplies from the Middle East.
Traders said supplies from the MidEast were tight where Bahrain has already sold out while Kuwait has only one spot cargo due for arrival in Asia early March.

They also said Indonesia would continue to be a healthy buyer of jet fuel as they buy ahead of the Haj pilgrimage due in mid-April. Indonesia has already bought a high 1.5-million barrels for February arrival.
Traders said despite good demand from the U.S. West Coast, the arbitrage has shut as Asian prices have risen by $2.00 a barrel over the past two weeks.
Some traders said they were largely sceptical about the jet fuel deal reported on Monday between a Swiss trader and a Singapore trader at $31.30 a barrel, free-on-board (fob) basis.
On Tuesday, the same Singapore trader was bidding at $31.10 per barrel and a major emerged to offer at the price. But by the day's end, no trade was reported.
Traders said they did not expect an improvement in gas oil prices until the second-half of February when they hope to see Chinese buyers re-emerge after their Lunar New Year break.
A European major bought a 150,000-barrel cargo offered by a Singapore trader at $24.80 per barrel fob lifting February 19-23, 50 cents below the last traded level on January 31.
